prompt: What really caused the 2008 financial crisis? Tell it as a story starting from the US housing boom, include subprime mortgages, securitization, Lehman Brothers and the government response.

plan.title: What Really Caused the 2008 Financial Crisis
plan.description: The 2008 financial crisis grew out of the US housing boom, subprime mortgages and securitization. It peaked with the fall of Lehman Brothers and a sweeping government response.

beats.narration: A bet on American homes nearly broke the world economy. Prices kept rising, so banks handed mortgages to almost anyone, even buyers who couldn't really afford them.

props.text: A bet on homes nearly broke the world.

beats.speaker: narrator

beats.narration: Those risky subprime loans were bundled together and sold to investors as supposedly safe securities. This was securitization. Lenders passed the risk along, so nobody cared who could repay.
beats.speaker: narrator

beats.narration: Then home prices fell. Borrowers defaulted, and those securities lost value. Banks holding them panicked, and in September 2008, Lehman Brothers collapsed.
beats.speaker: narrator

beats.narration: Credit froze worldwide. Governments stepped in, rescuing banks, cutting interest rates and spending heavily. The lesson: when everyone ignores risk, the whole system pays.
beats.speaker: narrator

warnings: length: the narration totals 102 words in 4 beats but a 45-second video needs about 89 (between 80 and 89). Cut about 13 words: 4 to 5 beats of about 22 words each (you averaged 25; count the words of every beat), one idea, no preamble and no recap; keep the hook and the last line
